title: Tiered decisioning playbook for passive activation and restore certification
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Purpose: Create an executable playbook and automated validation harness for active->passive promotion (passive activation) that enforces SLO gates, circuit-breaker behavior, and tiered load-shedding, plus a repeatable backup/restore certification workflow.

Goals:
- Define decision tiers and acceptance gates for promoting passive region(s) to active: health checks, KV/indices consistency, tokenstore integrity, and latency SLOs.
- Implement automated preflight validation that can be run as a CI-like pipeline prior to a scheduled drill or emergency promotion.
- Provide clear rollback and quarantine criteria driven by circuit-breaker signals and integrity checks.
- Integrate load-shedding policies so promoted passive can selectively drop non-critical traffic while preserving high-priority SLAs.
- Produce a documented schedule and checklist for quarterly drills, plus small canary drills that run weekly.

Scope (in):
- Passive activation steps for regional failover for the inference runtime and tokenstore.
- Automated snapshot verification and incremental restore smoke tests against a read/write canary workload.
- Integration with circuit breaker controller and routing layer to enact soft-fence and hard-fence actions.
- Telemetry dashboards and alert rules used as SLO gates.

Out of scope:
- Full cross-region database migration tooling.
- Long-term reconciliation jobs beyond the restore smoke window (these are follow-ups).

SLO gates (pre-promote & post-promote):
- Pre-promote: 99.9% successful snapshot restore within 15 minutes for the tokenstore subset used by the canary.
- Post-promote (first 30 minutes): p95 latency <= baseline_p95 * 1.4 and error-rate < 1%.
- If either gate fails, automatic rollback triggered and incident declared.

Decision tiers (unique to this playbook):
- Tier 0 (Automated Safe): All preflight validations green. Proceed with non-disruptive traffic siphon (canary routing) and scaled promotion.
- Tier 1 (Conservative): Minor telemetry anomalies (degraded p95 but error < 0.5%). Continue with aggressive load-shedding on best-effort routes and maintain rollback watch for 20 minutes.
- Tier 2 (Hold): Data integrity checksum mismatch OR error-rate >= 1%. Abort promotion, attempt staged rollback and run forensic snapshot compare.
- Tier 3 (Quarantine): Signs of KV divergence or tokenstore corruption. Mark passive as quarantine, failover to alternate region or activate capacity in dedicated pool.

Circuit breaker interplay and thresholds:
- Routing circuit breaker trips when error-rate > 2% for 1 minute OR sustained p99 latency > 3x baseline for 2 consecutive minutes.
- When tripped, route non-critical customers to fallback model variant and enact per-tenant soft limits.
- Auto-escalation: after 5 minutes of tripped state with no recovery, promote Tier 2 decision path and start restore-forensic job.

Load-shedding policy matrix (applied immediately post-promote if Tier 1 anomalies observed):
- High-priority routes (internal, premium): preserved, throttled but accepted.
- Medium-priority: apply token-based rate caps; requests over quota receive 429 with retry-after.
- Low-priority: immediate reject with explanatory structured error; cached responses served where available.

Automated validation harness (CI-style):
- Steps executed by pipeline: 1) snapshot integrity assert (checksums), 2) incremental restore to staging passive cluster, 3) run canonical canary generator (~10 concurrent user-sessions) for 20 minutes, 4) run heavy KV read-write fuzz tests for 5 minutes, 5) compute telemetry and verify SLO gates.
- Artifacts: stored logs, snapshot checksums, canary traces, and a signature file asserting pass/fail.

Runbook snippet (executable checklist):
- Owner on-call: SRE lead + Runtime infra engineer.
- 00:00 - Start preflight pipeline (link below).
- 00:15 - Verify snapshot checksums and tokenstore rehydrate output.
- 00:30 - Begin controlled traffic siphon (5% -> 25% -> 50%) to passive region using canary header.
- 00:45 - Monitor telemetry panel: p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, KV lag metrics.
- 00:55 - If gates remain green, increase to full traffic cutover. If Tier 1 anomalies detected, enable policy-based load-shedding and hold for 20 minutes.
- Rollback: trigger rollback playbook if Tier 2 or Tier 3 conditions met. Document snapshot IDs used.

Telemetry & alerting (quick list):
- Dashboard: DR Promotion Overview (queries: restore.duration, restore.success_rate, tokenstore.checksum_mismatch, request.latency_p95).
- Pager alert: DR-PROMOTE-FAILED if preflight pipeline fails.
- SLO alert: SLO-DEGRADED if p95 > baseline*1.4 for 10m.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- A machine-readable playbook (YAML checklist + step runner) committed to repo.
- Automated preflight pipeline added to CI with pass/fail artifacts.
- A scheduled drill configured in the runbook calendar and automation to execute weekly canaries and quarterly full drills.
- Post-drill report template and an initial drill completed in staging with signoff.

Links & artifacts referenced:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/DR+Tiered+Decisioning (draft)
- GitHub PR for harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1427
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dr-promotion-overview

Next steps:
- (Maya) implement checksum compare routine and add to restore pipeline.
- (Liam) wire up circuit breaker signal into promotion orchestrator.
- Schedule first staging drill week of 2025-09-29.

release_notes: Adds a tiered DR promotion playbook with an automated preflight validation pipeline and initial staging drill artifacts. This enables SLO-gated passive activations and configurable load-shedding policies.
postmortem_template: Post-drill report must include: drill scope, snapshot IDs, telemetry graphs, decision tier transitions, any rollbacks and root cause analysis, and action items with owners.
